title: Why he stayed in France in 1940; marriage to Georgina
summary: Briggs trusted the French army and, with a Belgian wife whom he married in 1930, he chose to stay rather than return; he became French only in 1955.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And the obvious question that comes up is why you chose to stay here, once you knew there was going to be a lot of trouble.
Well, yes, I personally did not believe that the French
Briggs
army was so weak. I thought that it would -- after World War I, they would make a much better stand, you see.
I had full confidence. And a certain reason is that my wife being Belgian, I thought I'd stay. You see, my wife, she didn't care so much for going back to the States.

Under those circumstances, 'cause we would both be, we said, 'not deported' but we would be sent back -- I had not much money -- plenty money to pay my fare, but if I went back, I would have gone back with the other boys that went back, were sent back by the Co[nsul], and then they would have a pretty difficult time to try to come back to France after the War if they wanted to, you see.
I see.
So, I decided to stay, but I paid [for it] (Laughter).
Well, when had you
Briggs
gotten married?
Huh?
When were you married?
I was married way back in '30, before I went to America.
And your wife, what was your wife's name?
Her name was Georgina Dagenner Briggs.
Dagenner was --
Dagenner, because she was Belgian. D-a-g-e-n-n-e-r.
So by this time you had been married for almost ten years?
Yes, and I --
Were you a French citizen then?
No, no.
Still American?
I only became a French citizen after, way back in '55.
Briggs
I see, I see. So you stayed here, and you just assumed that the French were going to be able to hold out?
Yes. That's all, yes.
